capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension — whether the features StorageView and the
prompts argument accept N stacked 30s mel windows in one call rather than
one call per window. The current code passes a single (1, n_mels, 3000)
feature and a one-element prompt list; I probed whether N>1 is supported.
what_i_learned:
generate(features, prompts) is batched: a (N, n_mels, 3000) feature tensor
(built by stacking per-chunk processor outputs) plus a length-N prompt list
returns N independent results, one decoded sequence per window. The leading
axis of input_features is a true batch dim, not a fixed singleton — so
long-form coverage costs one batched call, not N sequential calls.
hypothesis:
Window the raw audio into consecutive 30s segments, stack each segment's
mel features into one (N, n_mels, 3000) batch, decode all windows in a
single generate() call, and join the per-window text in order. This
eliminates the tail-deletion that the single-window stub suffers on every
multi-minute 0715 call, while batching holds runtime near the budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob decoding kwarg and the per-result
no_speech_prob attribute it populates. The docstring lists it among the open
decoding_kwargs, but every prior iteration read only result.sequences_ids and
threw the rest of each result object away. I studied what the result object
carries beyond the token sequence.
what_i_learned:
Passing return_no_speech_prob=True attaches a scalar no_speech_prob to each
batched result (one per stacked window), independent of the decoded tokens —
a confidence-of-silence signal the pipeline was discarding. This is a real,
free per-window VAD-style gate available straight from the decode call, no
extra model invocation or external silero asset needed.
hypothesis:
Stack all 30s windows into one batched generate (ledger-established) for full
long-form coverage, request no_speech_prob, and skip any window above 0.6 so
silence/hold-music regions stop contributing hallucinated text — cutting the
insertion/hallucination axis while deletions drop from no-longer-truncating.

capability_investigated:
The structure the generate() prompts argument accepts beyond a bare
start-of-transcript header — specifically whether a leading <|startofprev|>
segment carrying prior-context token ids is honored, i.e. Whisper's
condition-on-previous-text path through the frozen decode call.
what_i_learned:
The prompts list is not restricted to [<|startoftranscript|> <|lang|>
<|transcribe|> <|notimestamps|>]; it accepts a [<|startofprev|>, ...context
ids..., <|startoftranscript|>, ...] form so each window can be conditioned on
the previous window's decoded tokens. This conditioning is inherently
sequential (window N needs window N-1's output) so it cannot share iter_001's
batched single-call path — a genuinely different long-form mechanism.
hypothesis:
The stub decodes only one 30s window, deleting the entire tail of every
multi-minute call (deletion-dominant). Chunk into sequential 30s windows and
prefix each window's prompt with the previous window's re-encoded text via
<|startofprev|>, giving full coverage plus cross-boundary coherence to curb
boundary substitutions.

capability_investigated:
The per-result scores field on the generate() return object — the mean token
log-prob CT2 attaches to each decoded sequence (results[0].scores[0]) when
return_scores=True, which every prior iteration discarded while reading only
sequences_ids. Paired it with a zlib compression-ratio test on the decoded
text as a repetition detector.
what_i_learned:
generate(..., return_scores=True) populates result.scores: a list of one
mean-log-prob float per returned sequence, independent of no_speech_prob and
of the token ids. It is a free per-window decode-quality signal (low = the
decode lost the thread) that, combined with text compression ratio, lets the
pipeline detect a degenerate window and act on it without any extra model
surface — the canonical Whisper temperature-fallback trigger.
hypothesis:
The worst files are repetition collapses (repeated_text on cer 0.85–0.98),
and startofprev conditioning propagates a looped window into the next. Gating
on scores + compression ratio and re-decoding only the failing windows at a
rising sampling temperature should break the loops and stop feeding them
forward, lowering corpus_cer.

capability_investigated:
Whisper timestamp tokens through the frozen decode call: dropping
<|notimestamps|> from the SOT prompt so generate() emits <|t.tt|> timestamp
tokens, and reading them out of results[0].sequences_ids (ids >= the <|0.00|>
token id, each step above it = 0.02s). Every prior iteration forced
<|notimestamps|> and never inspected timestamp ids.
what_i_learned:
The prompt's <|notimestamps|> flag is optional, not mandatory — omit it and
the same generate() call returns timestamp tokens inline in the sequence. They
decode the model's own belief about where the last complete utterance ended
inside a window, which is exactly the seek signal the fixed 30s stride lacked.
This is a free coverage/boundary mechanism with no extra model surface.
hypothesis:
The dominant axis is coverage/deletion (length_ratio 0.79) with rampant
repeated_text — both consistent with a hard 30s stride cutting utterances at
the window edge. Replace the blind fixed stride with a timestamp-guided seek:
advance the next window to the last decoded timestamp (floored at half a chunk
to bound runtime), so straddling utterances are re-decoded whole instead of
sliced.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s repetition-control decoding_kwargs — repetition_penalty and
no_repeat_ngram_size — plus beam_size/patience, all listed as open kwargs in
the frozen backend docstring but never set: every prior iteration decoded
greedily (beam_size=1, no penalty), which is the canonical Whisper setup for
repetition collapse.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() pass-through forwards repetition_penalty and
no_repeat_ngram_size straight into ctranslate2.Whisper.generate, so the
decode call itself can suppress repeat-loop degeneration without any text
post-processing or extra model surface. Greedy beam_size=1 was leaving both
the repetition guard and beam search on the table.
hypothesis:
On the best pipeline (timestamp-seek longform, CER 0.4275) the four
highest-CER files are all repeated_text=true — a greedy repetition collapse.
Adding repetition_penalty=1.1 + no_repeat_ngram_size=3 breaks those loops and
beam_size=3 (patience 1.0) searches domain terms to cut the dominant
substitution axis, while a beam of 3 stays inside the runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt region as a carrier for a STATIC external lexical
prior (Whisper initial_prompt / hotword biasing), as opposed to iter_003's
use of it for self-generated previous-window text. Studied how the prompts
argument tokenizes and prepends arbitrary domain ids ahead of the SOT header,
and how the _MAX_PREV_TOKENS budget must be split between a fixed prior and
the running self-context.
what_i_learned:
The <|startofprev|> context accepts ANY token ids, not just decoded history —
a hardcoded domain glossary encoded via tok.encode(...) can lead the context
on every window, including window 0 (which previously had no prefix at all).
The decoder treats these as a vocabulary prior, so domain terms can be biased
without touching acoustics or adding model surface. The fixed prior and the
cross-window self-context coexist by reserving a token sub-budget for each.
hypothesis:
The dominant error axis is substitution (54%, length_ratio 0.96 healthy) =
domain terms mis-recognized over phone-band audio, not coverage. Seeding a
static insurance call-center glossary into the <|startofprev|> prefix biases
the decoder's lexical prior toward in-domain spellings on every window,
including the first, which self-conditioning alone cannot reach — directly
attacking the substitution headroom.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_alternatives + num_hypotheses decoding_kwargs and the
resulting multi-candidate shape of results[0].sequences_ids — i.e. the FULL
beam, not just the top hypothesis at index 0 that every prior iteration read.
what_i_learned:
With return_alternatives=True and num_hypotheses=N, results[0].sequences_ids
becomes a length-N list of complete decoded candidates (best-score first)
instead of a singleton, with a parallel results[0].scores list. The entire
beam is recoverable from one decode call — prior iters threw away N-1
hypotheses per window. This is a free per-window N-best surface, no extra
model invocation.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (54%) with healthy coverage, so headroom is in WHICH
candidate text wins, not how much is emitted. Walk the beam in score order and
skip any hypothesis whose zlib compression ratio exceeds 2.4 (repetition
collapse), taking the first coherent one — letting a runner-up beat a top beam
that degenerated, falling back to the top beam if all alternatives look bad.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt region as a STATIC domain-lexical prior (iter_007's
lever), composed with best/iter_006's repetition-controlled beam decode. I
studied how the prior's strength (term count x token budget) trades the
substitution gain against the insertion regression it caused at full size.
what_i_learned:
iter_007's domain prior is a strength-tunable lever, not binary: at ~40 terms /
budget 64 it improved substitution (0.54->0.52) and erased hallucination
(0.09->0.00) but forced unspoken terms (insertion 0.12->0.16). The bias is
monotone in prior size, so trimming to high-frequency terms and a small token
budget is the natural knob to keep the sub/hal gain while bounding insertions.
hypothesis:
Graft the domain prior onto best but shrink it to 16 high-frequency insurance
terms capped at 24 tokens, leading the <|startofprev|> context on every window
alongside the running self-context. A gentle prior should retain the
substitution/hallucination improvement on the dominant axis without re-inflating
insertions, netting below best's 0.1901 where the full-strength prior (0.1968)
could not.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s conditional re-decode control path: pairing return_scores
(mean log-prob per window, iter_004) with a zlib compression-ratio detector
to GATE a second decode of the same features at a different temperature —
the canonical Whisper temperature_increment_on_fallback mechanism. Prior
iters read scores/no_speech_prob as signals but never wired them into
control flow that acts (re-decodes) on a low-confidence window.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() pass-through can be invoked twice on the same
StorageView features with different decoding regimes (beam_size=3
greedy-temp vs beam_size=1 sampling_temperature=0.4 + sampling_topk), and
results[0].scores[0] from each call is directly comparable as a selection
criterion — so a per-window quality gate + recovery re-decode is fully
expressible through the frozen surface with no extra model method, just a
second call on the cached features. sampling_topk is a live, unused kwarg.
hypothesis:
Low mean-log-prob / high-compression windows are where the beam decode
derails into garbled substitutions (the dominant 55% axis, concentrated in
the worst files). Re-decoding only those windows with stochastic sampling
and keeping the higher-scoring transcript should recover substitutions
without touching the healthy majority of windows; a per-file cap of 4
bounds the extra decodes so runtime stays inside the 152s budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s suppress_tokens decoding_kwarg — a per-step logit mask of
forbidden token ids. Every prior iteration left it at the implicit default
[-1] (CT2's standard non-speech set) and never passed an explicit list; I
studied how -1 composes with appended ids and how the Whisper byte-level BPE
vocab (tok.get_vocab()) encodes script so a Latin-vs-Hangul partition is
cheaply derivable.
what_i_learned:
suppress_tokens accepts an explicit id list and CT2 keeps -1 as a sentinel for
its default non-speech suppression, so [-1] + extra_ids yields "default plus
mine". In Whisper byte-level BPE, ASCII a-zA-Z map to themselves while Korean
bytes map to high placeholder chars, so any get_vocab() key containing an ASCII
letter is a Latin-script token — a clean, fast (~50ms, no per-token decode)
partition. Specials/timestamps (keys starting with "<", all_special_ids) must
be excluded or the prompt header and timestamp-seek tokens get masked.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (55%) with healthy coverage; a real source on a Korean
call is cross-script leakage — Latin BPE tokens substituting for Hangul.
Forbidding the entire Latin-script token set at decode time removes that
failure mode without touching acoustics or adding model surface.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size kwarg under whisper-large-v3-turbo's specific
encoder/decoder layer asymmetry — i.e. the wall-clock cost of widening the
beam given that the turbo decoder is only 4 layers while the encoder it
shares per window is 32, so per-step beam expansion is cheap relative to the
once-per-window encode.
what_i_learned:
beam_size is a runtime-cheap knob on this backend: turbo's decoder is tiny
(4 layers) vs its 32-layer encoder, and the encoder runs exactly once per
window regardless of beam width, so going 3->5 multiplies only the cheap
decode path and stays inside the 152.3s budget — unlike on a full
large-v3 where decode dominates. Beam width is the natural focused lever for
the substitution axis here.
hypothesis:
With coverage healthy (length_ratio 0.97) and substitution dominant (55%),
the residual error is the decoder picking a near-homophone over the correct
in-domain token. Widening beam_size 3->5 (keeping the iter_009 domain prior,
repetition_penalty=1.1, no_repeat_ngram_size=3 fixed) gives beam search more
candidates to recover the higher-likelihood correct sequence, lowering
substitution without touching coverage or runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
model.detect_language(features) — a separate forward path on the
ctranslate2.models.Whisper object returned by frozen.load(). Every prior
iteration in the ledger only ever called generate(); I studied what methods
the load()-returned model object exposes beyond the decode call, and what
detect_language returns when handed the same StorageView features.
what_i_learned:
The object load() returns is the raw CT2 Whisper model, not just a decode
handle: it exposes detect_language(features), which returns one descending
list of (lang_token, probability) pairs per batched window — a free
acoustic language-confidence signal independent of generate()'s output. The
language token format matches the prompt tokens ("<|ko|>"), so the Korean
probability is directly readable, and it costs one encoder forward (cheap
vs decoding) so a once-per-file probe stays inside the 152.3s budget.
hypothesis:
Low Korean confidence correlates with garbled / phone-band audio, the
regime that drives the dominant substitution axis. Probe detect_language on
the first window and, when ko_prob < 0.85, raise the domain-prior budget
(24 -> 48) so the in-domain glossary fights substitution harder on exactly
the hard files, while confident-clean files keep the trimmed prior that
iter_009 showed avoids the insertion regression.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s length_penalty decoding_kwarg — CT2's exponential
sequence-length normalization in beam scoring, forwarded straight through
the frozen generate() pass-through. Every prior iteration left it at the
implicit default (1.0); I studied how it composes with beam_size to bias
hypothesis selection toward shorter/longer decodes.
what_i_learned:
length_penalty is a live, unused kwarg on the frozen surface: <1.0
down-weights longer beam hypotheses in the score normalization, which is
the direct lever against the insertion over-generation that widening the
beam (iter_012: beam=5 took sub 0.55->0.53 but insertion 0.13->0.15)
introduced. It is orthogonal to beam_size, so the two compose — wider beam
for the substitution axis, length_penalty<1 to guard its insertion cost.
hypothesis:
EXPLOIT-B tune on the dominant substitution axis: beam_size 3->4 buys more
search to recover phonetically-close mis-recognized tokens (the runtime-cheap
turbo lever from iter_012's ledger), and length_penalty=0.9 guards the
insertion regression that beam-widening alone caused in iter_012, kept gentle
so coverage (deletion 32%, length_ratio 0.97) is not depressed.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s N-best beam used as a CONTROL surface, not just observed:
return_alternatives=True + num_hypotheses=5 returns the full beam in
results[0].sequences_ids with the parallel results[0].scores list. iter_008
established the shape exists; I studied whether the per-hypothesis scores are
on a comparable scale to drive a custom selection rule (rerank), since every
pipeline including best/iter_009 still reads only sequences_ids[0].
what_i_learned:
The parallel scores list is a per-hypothesis mean-log-prob (best-first), so
the gaps between adjacent beams are small and directly additive — meaning an
external objective (decoder_score + λ·lexical_overlap) can re-order the beam
as a tie-breaker without a generation-time prior. This turns the discarded
N-1 hypotheses into a substitution lever: the correct in-domain term often
survives in a non-top beam even when the top hypothesis substitutes it away.
hypothesis:
Rerank each window's beam by decoder mean-log-prob plus a small per-domain-
term bonus (λ=0.05) and emit the argmax instead of index 0. Because it acts
only on already-decoded candidates it attacks the dominant substitution axis
(55%) while structurally avoiding the insertion regression that a stronger
<|startofprev|> prior caused (iter_009), since no unspoken term can be forced.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s patience decoding_kwarg — CT2's beam-search patience
multiplier, which extends how many finished hypotheses the beam waits to
collect (effectively patience x beam_size) before terminating, distinct
from beam_size which sets the search width. Every prior iteration including
best/iter_009 left it at the implicit/explicit 1.0; I studied it as the
depth lever orthogonal to the width lever beam_size.
what_i_learned:
patience is a live, unused-at-default kwarg that controls beam search DEPTH
independently of beam_size width. patience>1 lets the decoder keep exploring
finished hypotheses longer so a higher-likelihood sequence can overtake a
premature top beam, without the extra parallel beams that drove iter_012's
beam=5 insertion regression. On turbo's 4-layer decoder (iter_012) the added
search steps stay runtime-cheap, so deepening rather than widening is the
budget-safe way to attack the substitution axis.
hypothesis:
Raise patience 1.0->2.0 on the best beam-3 pipeline. The dominant axis is
substitution (55%) with healthy coverage (len 0.97); widening the beam fixed
some subs but cost insertions, so instead deepen the same width-3 search so
the correct in-domain term can win from a deeper path — a focused EXPLOIT
tune against substitution that should not reintroduce insertions.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames) — the forced
alignment method on the ctranslate2 Whisper object that frozen.load() returns.
Every prior iter called only generate()/detect_language(); align() is the one
decoder path never used. I studied what it consumes (a transcription-header
start sequence WITH <|notimestamps|>, a batched list of raw text token ids, and
encoder-frame counts) and what it returns per result.
what_i_learned:
align() returns a per-result WhisperAlignmentResult exposing text_token_probs:
one probability PER forced text token, audio-grounded (from the decoder forward
over the given text), and independent of generate()'s LM-weighted beam scores.
This is strictly finer than result.scores (a single sequence-mean log-prob,
iter_004): it localizes WHICH tokens the acoustics support. Cost: align
re-encodes the features (no encoder-output sharing with generate exists on the
frozen surface), so each call is ~1 extra 32-layer encoder pass — must be gated.
hypothesis:
On the dominant substitution axis, a fluent-but-wrong domain term can win a
near-tie on decoder score while the audio favours the runner-up. Decode top-2
(return_alternatives, num_hypotheses=2); only when the top-2 beam scores are
within _AMBIGUOUS_SCORE_GAP, forced-align the top hypothesis and, if its mean
text_token_prob < _AUDIO_PROB_FLOOR, emit hypothesis #2 instead. Ambiguity
gating keeps the extra encoder pass off most windows so the budget holds.

capability_investigated:
Composed two already-surfaced levers from the ledger: the <|startofprev|>
static domain prior strength knob (iter_007/iter_009 — monotone in prior
size) and generate()'s length_penalty kwarg (iter_014 — <1.0 down-weights
longer beam hypotheses in score normalization). No new backend mechanism
this exploit slot; I studied how the two interact in one decode call.
what_i_learned:
The two levers are mechanically coupled, not just orthogonal: a stronger
domain prior regresses by emitting EXTRA unspoken terms, which lengthens the
decoded sequence, and length_penalty<1.0 penalizes exactly that length axis
in beam scoring. So a length penalty is the natural same-call guard for the
prior's insertion regression — letting the prior be pushed back up toward
iter_007's strength (sub/hal gain) without paying iter_007's full insertion
cost, all inside the existing beam=3 budget.
hypothesis:
best/iter_009 over-trimmed the prior (budget 24) to dodge insertion, leaving
iter_007's sub (0.54->0.52) and hal (0.09->0.00) gains on the table. Restore
the fuller glossary at budget 48 and add length_penalty=0.9 to absorb the
resulting over-generation, so the dominant substitution axis improves while
insertion stays bounded.

capability_investigated:
model.align(features, start_sequence, text_tokens, num_frames) used as an
ACTIVE re-scorer, not just observed: iter_017 mapped that align() returns a
per-result WhisperAlignmentResult.text_token_probs (one audio-grounded prob
per forced text token, independent of generate()'s LM beam score) but it was
rejected before any measured pipeline used it. I wired it in: pull the full
beam (return_alternatives + num_hypotheses), and on contested windows align
every candidate's clean text ids against this window's tiled features.
what_i_learned:
align() is composable as a beam selector through the frozen surface: its
text_token_probs is on a per-candidate comparable scale, so mean(token_probs)
over each hypothesis re-orders the beam by ACOUSTIC support rather than LM
score — orthogonal to scores/length_penalty/lexical-overlap (iter_004/14/15),
all of which are LM- or text-side signals. The constraint is cost: align
re-encodes (no encoder sharing with generate on the frozen surface, iter_017),
so it must be gated; using the top-beam mean log-prob (iter_004) as the gate
confines the extra encode to genuinely low-confidence windows.
hypothesis:
On the substitution-dominant profile (sub 55%, length_ratio 0.97 healthy) the
errors are wrong tokens, not coverage. The LM-preferred top beam substitutes a
domain term the acoustics reject; a non-top beam often carries the right one
(iter_015). Selecting by audio-grounded align() prob on contested windows
should lower substitution where LM rescoring (iter_015) and length/prior
guards (iter_014/18) plateaued, while confident windows stay byte-identical to
best/iter_009 so runtime and the non-contested error mix are unchanged.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s max_initial_timestamp_index decoding kwarg — CT2's cap (in
0.02s timestamp steps) on how late the decoder may emit the FIRST <|t.tt|>
token. iter_005 surfaced that omitting <|notimestamps|> yields timestamp
tokens for the seek, but the constraint on the initial timestamp was never
touched; CT2's implicit default is 50 (=1.0s).
what_i_learned:
max_initial_timestamp_index is a live, unused-at-default generate() kwarg
that bounds where the decoder is allowed to place a window's first utterance
start. At the default 50 the decoder may declare up to 1.0s of leading audio
as pre-speech and skip it, shifting the acoustic alignment of everything
after — a window-head error source orthogonal to the global coverage axis
(length_ratio stays ~1.0 because the skipped lead is short). It directly
governs the same timestamp tokens iter_005's seek reads, so it is a finer
control on that mechanism rather than a new model surface.
hypothesis:
Cap the first timestamp at index 10 (~0.2s) instead of 1.0s. Each window
already seeks to an utterance boundary so true leading silence is small;
anchoring transcription near t=0 should reduce window-head substitutions
from the decoder skipping then re-aligning lead-in audio, without touching
coverage. Low-risk single-kwarg add to the existing beam/prior/seek decode.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size and length_penalty kwargs composed in one decode call —
iter_012 mapped beam width as a runtime-cheap substitution lever (turbo's
4-layer decoder), iter_014 mapped length_penalty<1.0 as the beam-score
length down-weight. I studied their interaction rather than a new mechanism.
what_i_learned:
beam=5 and length_penalty<1.0 are mechanically complementary: widening the
beam surfaces more sub-correcting hypotheses but lengthens/over-generates,
and length_penalty<1.0 penalizes exactly that length axis in CT2 score
normalization — so the insertion regression iter_012 paid for its sub gain
has a same-call guard that is orthogonal to beam width.
hypothesis:
Graft iter_012's beam_size=5 (sub 0.55->0.53) onto best/iter_009 and add
length_penalty=0.9 (iter_014) to suppress the insertion the wider beam
introduced, netting the substitution gain without the over-generation cost.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s patience kwarg (CT2 beam-search patience multiplier, iter_016)
applied as a focused EXPLOIT-B parameter tune on best/iter_009, which leaves
it at the default 1.0. No new mechanism — extracting value from a surfaced
lever against the dominant error axis.
what_i_learned:
patience controls beam-search DEPTH independently of beam_size width: at
patience>1 the decoder keeps collecting finished hypotheses longer so a
higher-likelihood sequence can overtake a premature top beam. Unlike beam=5
(iter_012/iter_022), it adds no extra parallel beams, so it should raise the
substitution-correcting selection pressure without the length/insertion
regression those width-widening attempts paid. On turbo's 4-layer decoder
the added search steps are runtime-cheap.
hypothesis:
The dominant axis is substitution (55%, length_ratio 0.97 healthy) — headroom
is in WHAT gets recognized, not coverage. Deepening beam search (patience
1.0->2.0) at fixed width=3 lets a better-scoring hypothesis displace the top
beam on contested in-domain/phone-band tokens, lowering substitution while
holding insertion/hallucination flat (no extra beams) and staying in budget.

capability_investigated:
The audio-side surface that load() returns alongside the model — the
WhisperProcessor feature extractor and the raw waveform handed to
processor(seg, sampling_rate=sr). Every one of the 23 ledger iterations
probed only the decoder (generate kwargs, the result object, model.align /
detect_language); the mel front end and its input were never examined.
what_i_learned:
The WhisperProcessor log-mel front end applies a fixed mel filterbank with
no pre-emphasis / spectral-tilt or AGC stage, and the waveform we pass to
processor() is a fully open, untouched input surface (transcribe receives a
raw np.ndarray we may transform before extraction, all still through the
frozen helpers — no forbidden import). So phone-band call audio reaches the
encoder with its native steep low-pass tilt intact; the only place to
correct that within the frozen surface is the waveform itself, since the
filterbank is fixed and inaccessible.
hypothesis:
Apply a first-order pre-emphasis y[n]=x[n]-0.97*x[n-1] to the full waveform
before windowing/feature extraction. The dominant axis is substitution
(55%, length_ratio 0.97 healthy) — acoustic mis-recognition, not coverage —
and flattening the phone-band tilt boosts the high-frequency consonant /
formant-transition cues that distinguish confusable Korean syllables, which
should lower substitution without disturbing the unchanged timestamp-seek
coverage path. Runtime cost is one O(n) numpy pass, negligible vs decode.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s length_penalty kwarg (iter_014) composed in one decode call with
the waveform pre-emphasis front-end surface (iter_024). No new mechanism — an
exploit-A synthesis of two already-surfaced levers that each moved a different
axis vs best.
what_i_learned:
Pre-emphasis and length_penalty are mechanically complementary, not just
co-applicable: iter_024's first-difference high-pass lifts high-frequency
consonant energy so the decoder hears more phonetic detail (sub 0.55->0.53),
but that extra detail also licenses more unspoken tokens (ins 0.13->0.15) —
a length increase. length_penalty<1.0 penalizes precisely the sequence-length
axis in CT2 beam-score normalization, so it is the same-call guard for the
insertion cost the acoustic correction pays, orthogonal to the mel front end.
hypothesis:
Apply _preemphasis(audio) before the processor's log-mel AND set
length_penalty=0.9 in generate(). The substitution axis dominates (55%) with
healthy coverage, so keep iter_024's acoustic sub-gain while neutralizing the
insertion regression that kept it from winning — net should clear best/iter_009.

capability_investigated:
The LEVEL/loudness axis of the raw-waveform input surface that load()'s
WhisperProcessor feeds: applying global RMS (AGC-style) normalization to the
np.ndarray before processor() mel extraction. iter_024 surfaced the waveform
as open and noted the fixed filterbank has NO AGC/level stage; iter_024/025

is a first-difference high-pass that reshapes the spectrum (consonant energy),

substitution-axis lever orthogonal to spectral tilt — and the only level
control available within the frozen surface, since the filterbank is fixed.

before windowing, so every file presents the encoder a consistent loudness;
with the substitution axis dominant and coverage healthy (len 0.97), more

and under-applies on its clip-saturated bands. The array is mutable in place

the speech spectral structure that also lives in the per-bin mean.

composed on the channel-EQ best, flattens the residual additive channel
coloration in the exact domain the encoder reads, reducing the consonant/vowel
substitution that dominates the error mix (55%) without touching coverage
(length-neutral, the seek still reads timestamps off the decoded sequence).

capability_investigated:
The input_features log-mel array load()'s WhisperProcessor returns between

which subtracted each bin's single GLOBAL temporal mean.
what_i_learned:

drift), so its log-mel offset is time-VARYING — the global-mean CMN (iter_088)
removes only the DC component and leaves the drift that smears consonant/vowel
identity (dominant 55% substitution axis). A local mean over ~150 frames
(~1.5s, computed per bin via one cumsum) subtracted from each trajectory
high-passes it: it removes that slow drift while keeping the 1-12 Hz phonetic
modulation. Critically, on a constant (near-silent) trajectory the local mean
equals the signal so the output is ~0, NOT amplified — the structural fix for
CMN's failure mode (insertion 0.13->0.22, hal 0.00->0.09 from amplifying
silent windows). The global mean is added back to preserve the encoder's
expected feature level; alpha=0.5 keeps the correction partial.

mel bin of input_features per window before to_storage_view, on top of the
channel-EQ best (iter_063). This removes the time-varying channel drift the
waveform EQ and global CMN both miss, attacking the dominant substitution axis
without the silent-window amplification that sank CMN.

The input_features log-mel array load()'s WhisperProcessor returns between
processor(seg) and to_storage_view() — treated as a per-mel-bin SECOND-MOMENT

none rescaled each bin's temporal variance.

A telephony codec compresses dynamic range non-uniformly across frequency, so
the channel scales the SPREAD of each mel-bin trajectory differently — collapsing
the spectral contrast that separates confusable consonants/vowels (dominant 55%
sub axis), which mean subtraction provably cannot restore (it shifts, never
rescales). CMVN's per-bin std rescale re-expands that contrast. Its lone risk is

windows into spurious speech (iter_091 hal 0.00->0.09); clamping each std to

scalars keeps the encoder's expected feature level. Budget-neutral, one numpy pass.

the variance normalization restores per-band dynamic-range contrast the
first-moment levers leave untouched, lowering substitution, while the std floor
+ partial blend hold off the silent-window over-generation CMN regressed on.
